structuredContent.latestTerminalSummary:
PP-OCRv6 is the strongest small OCR model Baidu has published, and it is not an independent state-of-the-art result. It came out on 11 June 2026. The weights are open. The training set that produced them is not.

**Release.** PaddleOCR 3.7.0 shipped PP-OCRv6 on 11 June 2026. The paper is [arXiv:2606.13108](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13108), submitted the same day by Baidu’s PaddlePaddle team. A Hugging Face write-up followed on 22 June 2026. OkuFlow’s GPU path uses the medium detector and medium recognizer from that release. Medium is the largest of the three tiers: about 34.5 million parameters in total, roughly 15.5 million for detection and 19 million for recognition.

**“SOTA” is their claim, on their test.** The paper says that on Baidu’s private in-house set, medium reaches 86.2% detection Hmean and 83.2% recognition accuracy, ahead of their own PP-OCRv5 server by 4.6 and 5.1 points, and ahead of Qwen3-VL-235B, GPT-5.5, and Gemini-3.1-Pro on that same OCR test. Those large models are general vision-language models, scored zero-shot. The test images, labels, and protocol are not public, so nobody else can rerun the table. Another Paddle page also warns that v5 and v6 numbers come from different sets. Two weeks earlier, on 28 May 2026, PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 claimed the lead on OmniDocBench. That is a different, much larger document parser, not this 34.5-million-parameter recognizer. Nothing in those papers measures a curled book page or a tilted on-screen panel.

**Training data.** The paper says v6 keeps the curated corpus from PP-OCRv5 and adds synthetic images plus real photos of industrial text: digital displays, dot-matrix type, tire markings, and power-adapter labels. It does not name a download, a size, or a license for that mixture. Paddle’s dataset guide lists public sets you can use to train your own model, such as ICDAR 2015, Total-Text, and CTW1500. Those are not the v6 training mixture. A public request in April 2026 for the PP-OCRv5 training set got no answer. The Apache-2.0 files on Hugging Face are the finished weights, not the pictures they were trained on.
structuredContent.summary:
Keep PP-OCRv6 medium detection and medium recognition on TensorRT. The paused book page and the tilted card are geometry and coverage problems, and a different recognizer would not repair them while the overlay still stretches upright text into axis-aligned boxes.

The report is commit `14bf18c61e5181c8a93dc10f14992eae1047ccd5` on `t3/ocr-engine-research`: `improvement_ideas/55-uct-ocr-engine-research-2026-10-21.md`. No application code, dependencies, or licenses were changed.

The tilted Clipchamp frame already has several correct strings (`Toggle`, `RightHand`, `LeftHand`). They are drawn as horizontal plates because the word rectangle discards the detector quad and the painter scales upright text with no rotation. The curled *Divina Commedia* page adds a second problem: one rotated rectangle around an arc overlaps the next line and warps the crop, which matches the fused tokens. Pan and zoom reproject words already accepted. They do not OCR the magnified pixels.

What is worth doing, in order:

1. Paint the existing quad with rotation, and compare our probability-map fitting with Paddle's contour quadrilateral on the same pinned medium map. The detector currently stops at 128 components per tile.
2. OCR the visible region at native resolution when the user pauses or zooms.
3. Only if the book is still unreadable, try UVDoc with boxes mapped back onto the original page.
4. Use docTR only as an offline word-polygon bake-off. Its published timings are CPU seconds on an i7, not a GPU result.

RapidOCR wraps the same Paddle weights. Windows OCR remains the fallback: one angle for the whole image and axis-aligned word boxes. Surya 2 and PaddleOCR-VL are the wrong latency class for live replacement, and Surya's weight license has a revenue cap. PP-OCRv5 server is behind v6 medium on Paddle's own table. There is no RTX 3050 measurement and no 120 FPS result. The report includes a frozen-frame protocol for coverage, false plates, geometry, cold and warm time, memory, and cancellation.
